internal_discovery.plain_explanation: The root smw appears 381 times and splits, with an exhaustive and clean morphological break, into two macro-fields that never once meet inside a verse. (A) The sky-stem samaa'/samaawaat (310) means the elevated created expanse above the earth: a built vault, the direction and source of what descends, and the upper term of the 'heavens-and-earth' totality. (B) The name-stem family (71) — ism/asmaa' (the borne/invoked designation), sammaa/tasmiyah (the act of naming), samiyy (namesake), musammaa (the lexicalized 'appointed term') — means a verbal designation attached to a referent, a label that may be true, empty, or even base. Nothing in the Quran bridges the two: no verse uses a sky-word to mean 'name' or a name-word to mean 'sky', no form-I 'to be high/ascend' verb of this root exists (height is always carried by other roots), and the one morphological bridge-candidate (samiyy, faEiyl) resolves inside the name-family as 'namesake' (19:7). The tempting single etymon 'elevation/height' is diachronic Arabic lexicography, forbidden here as authority, and is affirmatively disconfirmed internally (87:1 delegates highness to ʿlw, not to smw; idol-names are authority-less; ajal musammaa is a fixed due-date). The honest Quran-internal result is therefore not one nucleus but two coherent, unbridged classes.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: The root does NOT carry one unified meaning: 'sky' and 'name' share only the consonantal skeleton. Class A never entails naming/designation; Class B never entails sky, height, or ascent. A name (ism) does NOT entail truth, reality, or exaltation — it can be an empty human token (7:71, 12:40, 53:23) or blameworthy (49:11 بِئْسَ ٱلِٱسْمُ ٱلْفُسُوقُ). samaa' is NOT 'name', NOT abstract 'rank/highness', and NOT Paradise (janna is the reward-abode; 57:21 uses samaa' only as a measure of vastness). musammaa does NOT retain transparent 'named' — it is fossilized to 'appointed' and appears only with ajal. Boundary against the neighbour root smm: 7:40 سَمِّ ٱلْخِيَاطِ ('eye of the needle') is s-m-m, correctly absent from this packet — do not fold 'aperture' into smw.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: إِنْ هِىَ إِلَّآ أَسْمَآءٌ سَمَّيْتُمُوهَآ أَنتُمْ وَءَابَآؤُكُم مَّآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ بِهَا مِن سُلْطَٰنٍ (53:23; also 7:71, 12:40) — a name is nothing but an empty, authority-less human token — set against أَمِ ٱلسَّمَآءُ بَنَىٰهَا (79:27; 51:47, 21:32), where samaa' is the mightiest God-built physical reality. No contentful nucleus can span 'empty man-made word' and 'God-constructed firmament' without collapsing into vacuity; and where the text does pair a name with highness (87:1 ٱسْمَ رَبِّكَ ٱلْأَعْلَى) the highness is carried by a different root (ʿlw) on the Lord, not by smw on the name. This falsifies any 'elevation' bridge as a Quran-internal semantic (as opposed to historical) claim.
internal_discovery.strongest_competitor: The single-nucleus 'elevation/height' account (traditional lexicography, sumuww): samaa' = the raised expanse; ism = a mark 'raised' on a thing to make it known; sammaa = to set that mark; musammaa = marked-out/specified; samiyy = the exalted/co-marked; supported prima facie by 87:1 and 55:78 collocating ism with exaltation. It is morphologically economical and connects all classes. It is rejected as the operative SEMANTIC account on three Quran-internal grounds: (1) no verse demonstrates the bridge — it is imported diachrony, forbidden as authority; (2) the exaltation at 87:1/55:78 attaches to rabbika via the root ʿlw, not to the concept 'name' via smw; (3) it is affirmatively refuted by the empty idol-names (7:71, 12:40, 53:23), the base name (49:11), and the arbitrary due-date ajal musammaa (2:282, 71:4) — designations with zero height content. It may well be the historical origin, but that lies outside a Quran-internal semantic claim.
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: The single-nucleus 'elevation/height' account (traditional lexicography, sumuww): samaa' = the raised expanse; ism = a mark 'raised' on a thing to make it known; sammaa = to set that mark; musammaa = marked-out/specified; samiyy = the exalted/co-marked; supported prima facie by 87:1 and 55:78 collocating ism with exaltation. It is morphologically economical and connects all classes. It is rejected as the operative SEMANTIC account on three Quran-internal grounds: (1) no verse demonstrates the bridge — it is imported diachrony, forbidden as authority; (2) the exaltation at 87:1/55:78 attaches to rabbika via the root ʿlw, not to the concept 'name' via smw; (3) it is affirmatively refuted by the empty idol-names (7:71, 12:40, 53:23), the base name (49:11), and the arbitrary due-date ajal musammaa (2:282, 71:4) — designations with zero height content. It may well be the historical origin, but that lies outside a Quran-internal semantic claim.
internal_discovery.rationale: All three lenses independently reconcile the full 381 into the same exhaustive, morphologically clean 2-macro-class partition (A sky 310 / B name 71) and independently conclude there is NO Quran-internal bridge between them, with the 'elevation' etymon rejected as imported and internally disconfirmed. Per the contract ('same root != one meaning'; 'if two+ senses have no Quran-internal bridge, choose UNRESOLVED — do not force one nucleus'), the only honest root-level result is UNRESOLVED / multi-class: two internally-coherent but mutually unbridged fields. Within their own scopes each class is strong (A) or moderate (B, capped by the lexicalized ajal-musammaa sub-class and the thin samiyy base), but the ROOT does not license a single generalization. The sole bridge-candidate, samiyy, resolves inside Class B (19:7) and is retained as a RESISTANT seam. Note that A ('sky') and B ('name') are treated here as unbridged classes of one packet-root, not as a claim that either is THE root meaning.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: samaa'/samaawaat = the elevated created expanse above the earth: a built vault/roof/canopy, the source-direction of what descends (water, provision, punishment, angels, scripture), the adorned lower heaven of the stars, the 'up' direction and God's domain of decree, and (in the plural, ~183/190) the upper term of the 'heavens-and-earth' merism for the whole created order; ruptured at the eschaton.
clusters.classification_rationale: All 310 tokens carry the geminated sky-stem (s~amaA'-/s~ama`wa`t-) and cohere around one spatial/cosmological nucleus defined by contrast with al-ard. No token means 'name'; no ascent verb of this root exists (height/ascent is always carried by other roots: rfʿ, bny, ʿrj, rqy, ṣʿd).
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: Vault/roof: 2:22 ٱلسَّمَآءَ بِنَآءً, 21:32 سَقْفًا مَّحْفُوظًا, 51:47 بَنَيْنَٰهَا بِأَيْي۟دٍ, 55:7 رَفَعَهَا. Descent-source: repeated أَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءً (2:22, 6:99, 16:10). Merism: رَبُّ/غَيْبُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ (13:16, 49:18). Rupture: 82:1 ٱنفَطَرَتْ, 84:1 ٱنشَقَّتْ.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: ism/asmaa' = a name/appellation borne by a referent and invoked over it: the invocation formula (bismi, dhikr ismi llah over sacrifice), a person's assigned name (Yahya 19:7, al-Masih 3:45, Ahmad 61:6), God's 'beautiful names' as the means of address (7:180), the names taught to Adam (2:31) — and, polemically, the empty/base name (idols 7:71, fusuq 49:11).
clusters.classification_rationale: Nominal name-stem (ism/asmaa'); a linguistic designation attached to a referent, carrying NO entailment of truth, reality, or exaltation — a name may be groundless or blameworthy.
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: 1:1 بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ; 96:1 ٱقْرَأْ بِٱسْمِ رَبِّكَ; 7:180 ٱلْأَسْمَآءُ ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ فَٱدْعُوهُ بِهَا; 2:31 وَعَلَّمَ ءَادَمَ ٱلْأَسْمَآءَ كُلَّهَا; 7:71 أَسْمَآءٌ سَمَّيْتُمُوهَآ.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: sammaa (form II) / tasmiyah = the act of assigning or conferring a designation on a referent.
clusters.classification_rationale: Form-II causative/denominal of the name-stem plus its verbal noun; transparently derived from ism (to make/give a name).
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: 3:36 سَمَّيْتُهَا مَرْيَمَ; 22:78 هُوَ سَمَّىٰكُمُ ٱلْمُسْلِمِينَ; 13:33 قُلْ سَمُّوهُمْ; 76:18 تُسَمَّىٰ سَلْسَبِيلًا; 53:27 لَيُسَمُّونَ ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةَ تَسْمِيَةَ ٱلْأُنثَىٰ.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: samiyy = a namesake / one who shares the (same) name; the single morphologically tempting bridge-candidate toward 'lofty peer', but anchored to the name-family by its co-text.
clusters.classification_rationale: faEiyl form; 19:7 places it in apposition to ismuhu Yahya, forcing 'namesake'; 19:65 admits a residual 'peer/equal' reading and sits next to rabb al-samaawaat, which is the strongest pull toward unifying with the sky-stem. Thin base (2 tokens, both Sura 19); left RESISTANT to represent the unresolved A/B seam.
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: 19:7 ٱسْمُهُۥ يَحْيَىٰ ... لَمْ نَجْعَل لَّهُۥ مِن قَبْلُ سَمِيًّا; 19:65 هَلْ تَعْلَمُ لَهُۥ سَمِيًّا.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: musammaa = 'an appointed/specified term' — a fully lexicalized nominal sub-idiom bound to ajal in 100% of cases (أَجَلٍ مُّسَمًّى); drifted from transparent 'named' toward 'fixed/determined/set'.
clusters.classification_rationale: Passive participle (form II) of sammaa; never floats free of ajal, so it is a fossilized collocation. Coherent within itself as a designative extension ('to name a term' = to fix it), but no longer transparently 'named'.
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: 2:282 إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍ مُّسَمًّى (debt); 71:4 إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍ مُّسَمًّى (reprieve); 39:5 كُلٌّ يَجْرِى لِأَجَلٍ مُّسَمًّى (celestial bodies); 22:5 (womb); 30:8 (heavens created bi-l-haqq wa-ajal musamma).

reconciliation.rationale: Its residual 'peer/equal' reading, plus adjacency to رَبُّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ, makes it the single strongest internal temptation to unify the name-stem with the sky/height-stem. Because unifying is exactly what the evidence does NOT license, it is retained as a RESISTANT seam rather than smoothed into Class B.

It is the co-text that DISARMS the sole morphological bridge (faEiyl 'lofty one'); flagging it RESISTANT records that the bridge was tested and failed, which is the load-bearing fact behind the UNRESOLVED verdict.

Within its own lexicalized sub-idiom ('appointed term') it is fully coherent as a designative extension of naming (to name a term = to fix it); it does not break its cluster, but it does cap Class B below full unity and is recorded as a structural atypicality, not as class-breaking resistance.

adversarial_verification.notes: No single-nucleus falsification is run to PASSED because there is no unified root claim to defend; the root is reported as UNRESOLVED/multi-class. The unity hypothesis ('elevation') was actively probed and found not Quran-internally demonstrable (no bridging verse; height delegated to ʿlw at 87:1; idol-names and ajal musammaa carry zero height content), with the samiyy pair recorded as the residual resistant seam. NOT_REQUIRED is used per contract for an unresolved-class-only root.

occurrence_dispositions.candidate_semantic_interpretation: ism/asmaa' = a name/appellation borne by a referent and invoked over it: the invocation formula (bismi, dhikr ismi llah over sacrifice), a person's assigned name (Yahya 19:7, al-Masih 3:45, Ahmad 61:6), God's 'beautiful names' as the means of address (7:180), the names taught to Adam (2:31) — and, polemically, the empty/base name (idols 7:71, fusuq 49:11).

supporting_evidence.verse_text: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓا۟ إِذَا تَدَايَنتُم بِدَيْنٍ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍ مُّسَمًّى فَٱكْتُبُوهُ وَلْيَكْتُب بَّيْنَكُمْ كَاتِبٌۢ بِٱلْعَدْلِ وَلَا يَأْبَ كَاتِبٌ أَن يَكْتُبَ كَمَا عَلَّمَهُ ٱللَّهُ فَلْيَكْتُبْ وَلْيُمْلِلِ ٱلَّذِى عَلَيْهِ ٱلْحَقُّ وَلْيَتَّقِ ٱللَّهَ رَبَّهُۥ وَلَا يَبْخَسْ مِنْهُ شَيْـًٔا فَإِن كَانَ ٱلَّذِى عَلَيْهِ ٱلْحَقُّ سَفِيهًا أَوْ ضَعِيفًا أَوْ لَا يَسْتَطِيعُ أَن يُمِلَّ هُوَ فَلْيُمْلِلْ وَلِيُّهُۥ بِٱلْعَدْلِ وَٱسْتَشْهِدُوا۟ شَهِيدَيْنِ مِن رِّجَالِكُمْ فَإِن لَّمْ يَكُونَا رَجُلَيْنِ فَرَجُلٌ وَٱمْرَأَتَانِ مِمَّن تَرْضَوْنَ مِنَ ٱلشُّهَدَآءِ أَن تَضِلَّ إِحْدَىٰهُمَا فَتُذَكِّرَ إِحْدَىٰهُمَا ٱلْأُخْرَىٰ وَلَا يَأْبَ ٱلشُّهَدَآءُ إِذَا مَا دُعُوا۟ وَلَا تَسْـَٔمُوٓا۟ أَن تَكْتُبُوهُ صَغِيرًا أَوْ كَبِيرًا إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلِهِۦ ذَٰلِكُمْ أَقْسَطُ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ وَأَقْوَمُ لِلشَّهَٰدَةِ وَأَدْنَىٰٓ أَلَّا تَرْتَابُوٓا۟ إِلَّآ أَن تَكُونَ تِجَٰرَةً حَاضِرَةً تُدِيرُونَهَا بَيْنَكُمْ فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَلَّا تَكْتُبُوهَا وَأَشْهِدُوٓا۟ إِذَا تَبَايَعْتُمْ وَلَا يُضَآرَّ كَاتِبٌ وَلَا شَهِيدٌ وَإِن تَفْعَلُوا۟ فَإِنَّهُۥ فُسُوقٌۢ بِكُمْ وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَيُعَلِّمُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَٱللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَىْءٍ عَلِيمٌ

occurrence_dispositions.note: Nominal name-stem (ism/asmaa'); a linguistic designation attached to a referent, carrying NO entailment of truth, reality, or exaltation — a name may be groundless or blameworthy.
occurrence_dispositions.candidate_semantic_interpretation: ism/asmaa' = a name/appellation borne by a referent and invoked over it: the invocation formula (bismi, dhikr ismi llah over sacrifice), a person's assigned name (Yahya 19:7, al-Masih 3:45, Ahmad 61:6), God's 'beautiful names' as the means of address (7:180), the names taught to Adam (2:31) — and, polemically, the empty/base name (idols 7:71, fusuq 49:11).

layer_attribution.occurrence_evidence: 381 occurrences read/sampled with full coverage of every minority form; the sky-stem (310) and name-stem family (71) split with an exhaustive, morphologically clean break and never co-mean within any verse.
layer_attribution.derivation: Name-family derivations are transparent and mutually anchored (ism -> sammaa/tasmiyah -> samiyy -> musammaa), e.g. 7:71/12:40/53:23 co-locate asmaa' + sammaytumuuhaa in one clause; the sky-stem has no derivational tie to the name-stem and no form-I 'ascend' verb.
layer_attribution.lexical_class: musammaa is a fully lexicalized nominal sub-idiom bound to ajal (21/21) meaning 'appointed term'; it is a designative extension of naming but no longer transparently 'named', and it caps the name-family below full unity.
layer_attribution.contextual_relation: Where a sky-word and a name-word co-occur (2:31-33 asmaa' taught to Adam beside ghayb al-samaawaat; 19:7 ismuhu ... samiyy beside 19:65 rabb al-samaawaat ... samiyy) the text treats them as unrelated senses in proximity, never as wordplay or bridge; this contextual proximity must NOT be promoted into a root-level unity claim.
layer_attribution.reconciliation: The samiyy pair was preliminarily readable as settled Class-B 'namesake' but is finally retained as RESISTANT to mark the tested-and-failed bridge; the musammaa set was preliminarily RESISTANT to Class B but finally CONSISTENT within its own lexicalized sub-idiom while still capping B.
layer_attribution.unresolved_resistance: The root-level unity is UNRESOLVED: two coherent but Quran-internally unbridged classes (sky / name). The residual resistant occurrences are samiyy (19:7, 19:65); the 'elevation' etymon that would unify them is imported and internally disconfirmed (87:1, idol-names, ajal musammaa).

hard_cases.reason: samiyy readable as 'peer/equal' rather than 'namesake', adjacent to رَبُّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ; the single strongest internal temptation to bridge the name-stem to the sky/height-stem. Anchored back to name by 19:7, but the seam stays unresolved.

evidence_basis.statement: samiyy at 19:65 is the sole morphological bridge-candidate (faEiyl 'lofty one'), yet its 19:7 twin apposes it to ismuhu Yahya, forcing 'namesake'; adjacency to samaawaat is coincidental juxtaposition, not a Quran-internal derivation.

hard_case_representation.rationale: The root is UNRESOLVED/multi-class: two coherent but Quran-internally unbridged fields (sky vs name). The persisting resistance is the A/B seam itself, carried concretely by the samiyy bridge-candidate (19:7, 19:65) which is retained RESISTANT, and reinforced by the adversarial boundary occurrences (empty idol-names 7:71/12:40/53:23, base name 49:11, ʿlw-delegation 87:1, God-built firmament 79:27) that refute the tempting 'elevation' unifier. All final-RESISTANT occurrences (19:7, 19:65) are represented as RESISTANT_SEAM hard cases and listed in counterevidence_refs.

rejection_condition.challenging_finding: A single verse (or a demonstrable intra-root pattern) in which the sky-stem and the name-stem semantically bridge — e.g. a samaa'-word used to mean 'name/designation' or an ism-word used to mean 'sky/height', or samiyy at 19:65 shown to mean 'lofty peer' via a sky/height collocate rather than 'namesake' — which would license partitioning the root under one nucleus instead of two unbridged classes.
rejection_condition.search_location: The samiyy pair (19:7, 19:65) against their samaawaat co-text; the ism+height collocations (87:1, 55:78); the musammaa set (all 21 ajal tokens); and any verse co-locating a sky-word and a name-word (2:31-33; 19:7 vs 19:65).
rejection_condition.verification_method: Read each candidate verse's Tanzil text and QAC morphology (qac_pos, qac_verb_form, surface stem) and require the bridging sense to be predicated WITHIN the verse by the root itself, not supplied by a neighbouring root or by external lexicography.
rejection_condition.confounder_control: Exclude diachronic etymology (sumuww) and classical lexicon glosses as authority; exclude highness supplied by ʿlw/rfʿ and coincidental juxtaposition (adjacency of samiyy to samaawaat at 19:65 is not a derivation); confirm 7:40 سَمِّ ٱلْخِيَاطِ is root smm, not smw.
rejection_condition.failure_consequence: If such a bridge is demonstrated, the UNRESOLVED/multi-class verdict is withdrawn and the root is re-graded toward a single-nucleus ROOT_GENERALIZATION; if not, the two-unbridged-class result stands.

reopen_conditions: A Quranic occurrence is found in which a samaa'/samaawaat (sky-stem) word carries a naming/designation sense, or an ism/asmaa'/sammaa (name-stem) word carries a sky/height sense, establishing an intra-root semantic bridge.
samiyy at 19:65 is shown, on Quran-internal grounds, to mean 'lofty peer/equal' via a height collocate of this root rather than 'namesake', reconnecting the name-stem to the sky-stem.

A form-I verb of smw meaning 'to be high / to ascend' is identified in the corpus, or an ism+height predication is shown to use smw itself rather than ʿlw (contra 87:1), supplying the missing elevation bridge.
The musammaa sub-class is found outside the fixed ajal collocation with a transparent 'named' sense, changing the internal structure of the name-family.

falsification_evidence.status_rationale: No single-nucleus falsification is run to PASSED because there is no unified root claim to defend; the root is reported as UNRESOLVED/multi-class. The unity hypothesis ('elevation') was actively probed and found not Quran-internally demonstrable (no bridging verse; height delegated to ʿlw at 87:1; idol-names and ajal musammaa carry zero height content), with the samiyy pair recorded as the residual resistant seam. NOT_REQUIRED is used per contract for an unresolved-class-only root.
